rmt-2009-calc-02.prompt: At RMT 2009 is a man named Bill who has an infinite amount of time. This year, he is walking continuously at a speed of $\dfrac1{1+t^2}$, starting at time $t=0$. If he continues to walk for an infinite amount of time, how far will he walk?

rmt-2009-calc-05.prompt: Let $a(t)=\cos^2(2t)$ be the acceleration at time $t$ of a point particle traveling on a straight line. Suppose at time $t=0$, the particle is at position $x=1$ with velocity $v=-2$. Find its position at time $t=2$.
rmt-2009-calc-05.reviewNote: Official key gives (33-cos 8)/32, which drops the t^2/4-2t terms of the position at t=2; the correct value -(63+cos 8)/32 (about -1.964) was confirmed by numerical integration.

rmt-2009-calc-08.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_0^\infty4\lfloor x+7\rfloor e^{-2x}\,dx$. Remember to express your answer as a single fraction.

rmt-2009-calc-10.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^\infty\frac1{50+n^2/80000}$ as a decimal to the nearest tenth.
